method: Restart from the published CSZ definitions of normal subcase, L_P, axiom (v), and Lemma 10, plus the published List-3 Claims 14-16. Do not import the primary result's prose argument.
independent_derivation: Take any attempted compiled normal subcase P' and any vertex v outside S' union X0'. By CSZ definition, L_{P'}(v) depends only on colored neighbors in S'.

Suppose an imported List-3 palette removes color c from v only because a neighboring singleton-colored vertex u is represented in X0'. Then u is not counted in N(v) intersect S', so that removal is absent from L_{P'}(v).
Hence external palette size <=2 does not imply source |L_{P'}(v)|<=2.
Axiom (v) requires a vertex with source list size 3 to lie in Y.
Lemma 10 independently recomputes the canonical partition from source list sizes and assigns source-size-3 vertices to Y=Z3.
Therefore direct storage of bulk singleton restrictions in X0' cannot by itself compile the external palette reduction into the source X/Y partition.

The only generic escape routes are additional commitments (move v itself to X0'), additional seed witnesses (move suitable vertices to S'), or source-specific removal/decomposition. None of these is guaranteed by the published List-3 restriction theorem alone.

witness_recheck.family: S={a,b}; X0={x_j}; Y={y_j}; Y0={z_j}; edges ab,a-y_j,x_j-y_j,y_j-z_j; colors 1,2,3 as in the primary artifact.

limitations: Does not prove that no source-specific compilation can ever exist.
Does not invalidate auxiliary use of the P7-free List-3 algorithm.
Does not analyze the common d=1 refinement gate.
Does not promote the full-component quotient lemma.
